reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) concerns a different alloy (FeNiCoCrMo0.5Al1.3) and focuses on in-flight oxidation during HVOF spraying and isothermal annealing at 800°C, not on a controlled pre-oxidation treatment of a CoCrFeNiAl bond coat at 950–1050°C. It does not provide specific support for the key premises about the formation, barrier function, or durability improvement of the proposed alumina layer under the stated conditions.
premises: Controlled pre-oxidation of a CoCrFeNiAl bond coat at 950–1050°C in diluted oxygen yields a uniform, dense, alumina-rich layer.
The alumina layer acts as an effective diffusion barrier against oxygen ingress and metal cation migration.
The diffusion barrier mitigates further oxidation and spallation under high-temperature cyclic exposure.
The treatment improves durability relative to an untreated baseline under 1100°C cyclic oxidation in air.
